target_customer: Owners and operators of multi-tenant rental properties who want to earn money and savings from on-site energy assets and grid programs
problem: Tenants in rental buildings were locked out of the home battery and demand response boom, so rental property owners could not monetize flexible load or storage as virtual power plants.
business_model: B2B software and services for property owners, tied to energy savings and grid program revenue share (not confirmed by a primary source)
product_category: Virtual power plant software for multifamily and rental buildings

founders.name: Greg Sirotek
previous_startups: A proptech startup (name and outcome not stated on the YC page)

founders.name: Ross Gruber
founders.background_notes: Lead data engineer and engineering manager at prior startups.

competitors.name: Wasatch Energy Group with sonnen
competitors.what: Apartment complex battery virtual power plant projects in California
competitors.traction_then: Announced a fleet of about 3,000 apartment homes in 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed device and meter integrations plus utility and grid program enrollment across rental buildings, which is standard engineering with hard integration and regulatory parts for a team of six.

defensibility.rationale: Software layer on top of other vendors' hardware and utility programs, with no cited proprietary data or exclusive access.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A multi-tenant solar and EV billing company, Ivy Energy, absorbed it in October 2024.

market_need_then: A 2020 era press piece noted that tenants had largely been locked out of the home battery boom, and apartment VPP projects were being announced, which points to unserved rental demand. No Glow specific customer evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: glowenergy.com later redirected to a domain for sale page, so the exact .com was not retained after the acquisition (observed 2026-11).

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, sustainability focused (from the YC description)

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found. Searches for the name returned several unrelated Glow companies, including a solar company and a beverage brand.

outcome_analysis: Glow Energy was a six person Winter 2022 company selling virtual power plant software to rental property owners. It was acquired by Ivy Energy in October 2024 with undisclosed terms, and the release framed the deal as adding Glow technology and customers to Ivy's solar and EV billing platform. The cause of the exit, whether a strategic win or a soft landing after limited funding, is not public.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights and VCBacked (both aggregators) list about 500K USD in a June 2022 seed from Y Combinator and 10x Value Partners, so it is not recorded as a round. A 30M USD Glow round in search results belongs to a different solar company. Competition list is thin and predates the batch; no launch coverage dated near W22 was found.
